distinguishing_features: Uses internal enclosure pressure rise from gas evolution as leading indicator of electrolyte dry-out, not vapor-space thermal expansion coefficient anomalies to detect seal leaks
Targets electrolyte decomposition in sealed electronics enclosure (streetlight driver), not floating-roof tank seal integrity
Threshold derived from ideal-gas gas-moles calculation tied to decomposition products (H2/O2), not from isochoric dP/dT deviation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Detect electrolyte degradation/dry-out in a sealed enclosure early enough to intervene, using only existing internal pressure and temperature telemetry, without false alarms from ambient temperature swings.
parsed.viable_reason: Ideal-gas pressure rise from ~1 mmol gas evolution (~27.6 kPa) exceeds sensor resolution at the stated 0.1 L scale, and the test protocol with pass/fail and kill criteria is executable with existing sensors.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Repurposing internal enclosure pressure as a leading indicator of electrolyte dry-out via decomposition gas evolution is not a routine parameter tweak of the closest art's vapor-space thermal-expansion seal-leak inference, despite sharing the ideal-gas relation.
